Michelin Restaurants Bangkok 2026
Every Star + How to Book
intro: Bangkok is ASEAN's Michelin capital — 41 of Thailand's 43 starred restaurants are here. This page covers every one of them plus what other pages leave out: real prices, restaurant-by-restaurant booking steps, how fast you need to move, dress codes, and the nearest BTS
chips: 💡 Full booking info for every restaurant

blocks.html:
2026 is the first year Bangkok has held two three-star restaurants at once — Sorn still stands alone for Southern Thai food, and Sühring just moved up to join it. Right behind them come 8 two-star restaurants spanning royal Thai cuisine, modern Indian, riverside French, and farm-to-table in the middle of the city

We've ranked the 10 top-starred restaurants first, with everything you need to know before booking each one, then closed with a table covering all 31 one-star restaurants and their prices, booking method, and nearest BTS — tap 🔖 to save any restaurant straight to your trip plan from the card

blocks.name: Sorn
blocks.descHtml:
Sorn is the restaurant that made the world pay attention to Southern Thai food. Chef Ice — Supaksorn Jongsiri — opened it on Sukhumvit Soi 26 back in 2018 and took Southern Thai cuisine far enough to become the first restaurant in Thailand to win 3 Michelin stars (2025 guide), a rank it held onto again in the 2026 guide. The meal here is a tasting menu of 20-plus small Southern courses that walk you through the ingredients of the south's seas and gardens dish by dish, with Southern crab curry as the one dish everyone keeps talking about

The hard part about Sorn isn't the price — it's getting a table. The restaurant seats only about 22, so booking has become a monthly race. The TableCheck system opens for the following month at exactly noon Thailand time on the 25th of each month (moved to the 24th if the 25th falls on a Saturday), while overseas guests can email in from midnight on the 15th. The most serious advice is simply to set an alarm. The tasting menu runs 7,800++ THB per person (roughly 9,180 THB after service charge and tax), must be paid in full at the time of booking, cannot be cancelled or rescheduled under any circumstances, and any arrival more than 30 minutes late forfeits the table automatically. The restaurant serves dinner only, from 18:00 (closed Saturdays), and asks for smart elegant dress to match the occasion. It's about a 15-minute walk from BTS Phrom Phong, or a short taxi into the Soi Ari (Sukhumvit 26) lane. One key thing to know: the kitchen cannot adjust the menu for shellfish allergies or vegetarian diets

If you already love Southern Thai food, this is the most refined version you'll find anywhere in the country. Plan a month ahead, be ready on booking day, and you'll understand why this table is worth every alarm you set for it

Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Southern crab curry within a 20-plus-course Southern Thai tasting menu that walks through the region's ingredients dish by dish
blocks.bestFor: A major celebration meal for lovers of Southern Thai food who can plan a month ahead
blocks.hours: Dinner only, from 18:00; official Instagram bio lists servic

blocks.name: Sühring
blocks.descHtml:
Sühring is the restaurant of German twins Thomas and Mathias Sühring, who set up modern German cooking in a restored 1970s villa down Soi Yen Akat 3 in the Sathorn area. It's been open since 2016, and reached a moment many had been waiting for when the Thailand Michelin Guide bumped it up to 3 stars in the 2026 guide (announced November 2025) — making it the first German restaurant in Asia to hold 3 Michelin stars, and it also landed at No. 18 on Asia's 50 Best 2026. The most talked-about dish is Wildpastete, a wild-game pâté wrapped in pastry in true German style, alongside Spätzle with white Alba truffle and a reimagined Black Forest cake that closes the meal memorably

The tasting menu comes in two lengths, priced at 7,800 THB and 9,800 THB (the longer version runs about 7 courses), with a wine pairing adding another 5,800–9,800 THB depending on the tier you choose. Booking runs through SevenRooms up to 60 days in advance, and since the third star landed, weekend tables have been selling out within minutes of the booking window opening — the restaurant itself recommends booking at least a month ahead. One shortcut worth knowing: lunch, served only Thursday–Sunday 12:30–14:30, is far easier to book than dinner. One thing to watch for — cancelling within 48 hours or not showing up may incur a fee of 5,800 THB per person. Dress is smart casual, with the restaurant asking men to wear long trousers and proper shoes

The location sits down a quiet residential lane in the Yen Akat area, with no nearby train — BTS Chong Nonsi and MRT Lumphini are both about 2 kilometers away. A roughly 10-minute taxi from Sathorn is far easier than walking. If you're curious how German food climbed all the way to 3 Michelin stars, set an alarm for the 60-day booking window and go find out for yourself — this meal earns every bit of the planning

Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Wildpastete, a wild-game pâté wrapped in pastry in traditional German style — the signature dish that carried the Sühring twins to 3 Michelin stars
blocks.bestFor: A major celebration meal for those who can plan a month ahead

blocks.name: Gaa
blocks.descHtml:
Gaa is the restaurant of chef Garima Arora, the first Indian woman in history to win a Michelin star — and she did it in the very first year the restaurant opened, in 2017, after passing through legendary kitchens including Noma in Copenhagen and Gaggan in Bangkok. A second star followed in the 2024 guide and has held through 2026, and she also won the Thailand Michelin Guide's Young Chef Award in 2022. The restaurant moved from the Lang Suan area to a renovated Thai house on Sukhumvit Soi 53 in Thonglor back in 2021, giving it the feel of dining at a friend's house who happens to be an exceptional cook. The food here pairs Indian technique with Thai ingredients in bold ways — the dish everyone in town talks about is the charcoal-grilled durian "Tandoori Story" served with roti, alongside young jackfruit with pickled vegetables and roti, which has become another signature

Budget for the Gaa Experience tasting course at 6,200++ THB per person (raised from 5,200 THB as of July 1, 2026). Vegetarians get a full separate tasting menu at 5,200++ THB, genuinely built from scratch rather than just pulled meat off the standard plates. Dinner runs daily from 17:30, and weekends add a lunch service plus a 1,800 THB afternoon tea starting at noon. Kids age 7 and up are welcome (with a 2,000 THB kids' menu). Booking runs through TableCheck with prepayment; cancel free up to 48 hours before the meal (24 hours for afternoon tea), though no-shows are charged in full, and any dietary restrictions need at least 24 hours' notice. This is an all-tasting-menu restaurant, so walk-ins are essentially impossible — always book ahead. It's an easy trip: get off at BTS Thong Lo and walk about 7 minutes into the soi, and there's no strict dress code beyond dressing to match the occasion

If you want a two-star meal you can actually book without setting an alarm to race other diners like some of the famous names, Gaa should be one of the first names that comes to mind — especially with a vegetarian in your group, this meal turns into the kind everyone argues over afterward about which dish was best

Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Charcoal-grilled durian "Tandoori Story" served with roti — the dish that sums up Gaa in one bite
mustOrder: Young jackfruit with pickled vegetables and roti
blocks.bestFor: A special celebration meal, and vegetarians who want a full fine-dining tasting experience
blocks.hours: Dinner daily from 17:30; lunch + afternoon tea Sat–Sun from

blocks.name: Anne-Sophie Pic at Le Normandie
blocks.descHtml:
Any history of French fine dining in Thailand has to start in this room — Le Normandie was the country's first French fine-dining restaurant, open since 1958 on the top floor of the tower wing at the Mandarin Oriental hotel, with an uninterrupted view over the Chao Phraya River. Then in September 2025, the legend opened a new chapter when Anne-Sophie Pic, the female chef holding the most Michelin stars in the world, took over the kitchen, alongside a full renovation by design team Humbert & Poyet. The result showed up immediately — the 2026 Thailand Michelin Guide jumped the restaurant straight from 1 to 2 stars. The most talked-about dish is Berlingots, the small stuffed pasta parcels that are Chef Pic's personal signature, paired with dashi lobster served with red fruit

Budgeting is straightforward: a 3-course lunch runs 4,500++ THB, while dinner is the 7-course "Voyage" tasting menu at 9,000++ THB (à la carte is also available, with a minimum of 3 dishes per person). Book through the SevenRooms system on the Mandarin Oriental's website, and read the terms carefully — cancellations need 48 hours' notice or you'll face a fee of 2,250 THB per person for lunch or 4,500 THB per person for dinner. Groups of 6 or more should contact the hotel directly, and any food allergies also need 48 hours' notice. The dress code is properly formal — men must wear a jacket for dinner (don't worry if you forgot one, the restaurant has loaners), and sleeveless tops aren't allowed. The restaurant is open Wednesday to Sunday, lunch 12:00–15:30 (last order 13:30), dinner 18:30–23:30 (last order 21:00) — and note that in 2026 the restaurant closes annually from July 6–28, so don't plan around that window

Getting there is easier than it sounds — get off at BTS Saphan Taksin and walk about 10 minutes, or if you're already staying at the hotel, take the boat to Oriental Pier for a riverside feel before you even reach the table. For any meal that calls for something truly special — a proposal, an anniversary, or bringing someone important to a room with nearly 70 years of history — book here and you'll understand why the 2 stars arrived so fast

Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Berlingots, the small stuffed pasta parcels that are Anne-Sophie Pic's personal signature, now on the banks of the Chao Phraya
mustOrder: Berlingots, Chef Pic's signature stuffed pasta
blocks.bestFor: A major celebration meal — proposals, anniversaries, or a Chao Phraya-view dinner to remember for a lifetime

blocks.name: Chef's Table (lebua)
blocks.descHtml:
On the 61st floor of the State Tower at the lebua hotel sits a 2-Michelin-star contemporary French restaurant literally named for its concept — Chef's Table, because the heart of the place is the open kitchen where chef Vincent Thierry cooks in full view around a Molteni stove wrapped entirely in Carrara marble. As all seven courses arrive, you'll watch the Bangkok skyline through the glass at the same time, a meal that pairs French kitchen craft and city views at an equally high level, and the 2026 Thailand Michelin Guide confirmed the 2 stars again

The main event is the 7-course signature menu at 9,200++ THB (plus 10% service and 7% VAT). For the full experience there's a 7-glass wine pairing for another 8,800++ THB, with special upgrade options like Château Pavie or Château d'Yquem. Book through TableCheck, lebua's own system, or call +66 2 624 9555 / WhatsApp. The good news is this one is far easier to book than Sorn or Sühring — availability usually opens up just days to a few weeks out, with no need to set an alarm for a monthly race. What really matters is the dress code: men need a collared shirt and long trousers — no T-shirts, sleeveless tops, shorts, or hats, or you risk being turned away right at the Tower Club lobby. Getting there is easy — get off at BTS Saphan Taksin and walk about 10 minutes, but allow extra time to clear the lobby and take the elevator up to the 61st floor

If you want a 2-star French dinner with a view over all of Bangkok without racing to book months out, this is the one you can actually plan for someone special — just dress within the rules and head up

Read the full review →
blocks.area: Silom / Bang Rak riverside (State Tower, 61st floor)
blocks.signature: A 7-course contemporary French tasting menu cooked fresh at chef Vincent Thierry's open Molteni-stove kitchen
blocks.bestFor: A special-occasion dinner for anyone who wants both starred French cooking and a 61st-floor view of Bangkok

blocks.name: Côte by Mauro Colagreco
blocks.descHtml:
Côte is the restaurant of Mauro Colagreco, the Argentine chef behind Mirazur, the three-Michelin-star restaurant on the French Riviera coast that once topped The World's 50 Best Restaurants list. He opened Côte inside the Capella Bangkok hotel on the Chao Phraya riverside in the Charoenkrung area back in 2020, and sent Davide Garavaglia — who had been with the Mirazur kitchen since 2015 — to run the Bangkok kitchen himself. The food here reinterprets Riviera classics, with the menu changing daily based on what comes into the kitchen, all while you watch the Chao Phraya flow past. The restaurant moved up to 2 Michelin stars in the 2025 guide and held the rank through 2026

The main menu is the 9-course Carte Blanche at roughly 7,800 THB per person (plus 10% service and 7% VAT), but the shortcut worth knowing is the 4-course Escapade lunch at roughly 3,300 THB, which Time Out named Bangkok's best fine-dining lunch — same kitchen, same 2 stars, for under half the price of dinner. The restaurant is open Wednesday to Sunday, lunch 12:00–14:00 (last order 13:30), dinner 18:00–22:00, closed Monday–Tuesday. Book online via SevenRooms or through the Capella hotel directly. Weekend dinners fill faster than weekdays, but it's still far easier to book than a name like Sorn or Sühring. Getting there means getting off at BTS Saphan Taksin and walking along the riverside for about 10–15 minutes, or a short taxi into Capella. Smart casual is fine

If you're after a riverside special-occasion meal, or curious what food from the Mirazur family tastes like without flying to France, start with the Wednesday-to-Sunday lunch here — then you'll understand why the window-side tables always get booked first

Read the full review →
blocks.signature: 9-course Carte Blanche reinterpreting Riviera classics, with the menu changing daily based on ingredients
blocks.bestFor: A riverside celebration meal, and anyone who wants to try a two-star kitchen at lunch prices

blocks.name: R-Haan
blocks.descHtml:
R-Haan is a 2-Michelin-star Thai restaurant co-founded by chef Chumpol Jangprai, one of the best-known Thai chefs in the country. The heart of the restaurant is the word "samrub" — the traditional Thai way of eating, where several dishes are set at the center of the table for everyone to share, rotating with Thailand's three seasons, so summer, rainy-season, and winter samrub sets mean no two visits taste alike. Consistency is where this restaurant really earns its keep — it has held 2 Michelin stars every single year since the 2020 guide through 2026. It's located at 131 Sukhumvit Soi 53 (Soi Paidee Madee) in Thonglor

Budget roughly 5,212++ THB per person for the seasonal samrub set (2025-era reviews list 5,212–5,512 THB), with a wine pairing adding roughly another 3,512–3,812 THB. The restaurant serves dinner only, daily 18:00–23:00, and books through TableCheck with a deposit required to confirm the table. Groups over 5 should contact the restaurant directly at 095-141-5524; there are private rooms for 6 and 18 guests for family meals or hosting, and children age 6 and up are welcome. Dress is smart casual — men should wear long trousers and closed-toe shoes, with no sportswear, sandals, or sleeveless tops. As for getting there, the restaurant sits deep in the soi, about a 15-minute walk from BTS Thong Lo — a taxi or motorbike taxi the rest of the way beats the long walk

If you're after a special meal to show someone you love, or a foreign guest, what real traditional Thai cooking actually looks like, book a samrub set here for a night — and don't miss the traditional river prawn tom yum kung that everyone brings up in the same breath

Read the full review →
blocks.area: Thonglor (Soi Paidee Madee, between Sukhumvit 53 and Thonglor Soi 9)
blocks.signature: A seasonal Thai samrub set that rotates through three seasons, served family-style, with a whole river prawn tom yum kung as the most talked-about dish
mustOrder: Traditional river prawn tom yum kung
blocks.bestFor: A special-occasion meal, and introducing foreign guests to authentic Thai cuisine
blocks.zone: Thonglor (Soi Paidee Madee, between Sukhumvit 53 and Thonglor Soi 9)

blocks.name: INDDEE
blocks.descHtml:
INDDEE is a contemporary Indian tasting-menu restaurant tucked inside a beautifully restored century-old townhouse down a small lane off Lang Suan. The kitchen is led by chef Sachin Poojary, formerly Chef de Cuisine at Wasabi by Morimoto in New York, who takes Indian food far beyond the curry-house image most people carry around. The restaurant just launched its newly developed "Chapter Three" menu in late July 2025, and the payoff was immediate — the 2026 Thailand Michelin Guide moved it from 1 to 2 stars this year. For wine drinkers, this is also a real destination: its wine program won Star Wine List of the Year in 2023 and a Wine Spectator award in 2024

The menu is built as a "journey" across India's regions — choose between the 8-Destination Journey at 4,200++ THB or the 10-Destination Journey at 4,900++ THB, with an all-vegetable version of the long course also available at 4,200++ THB. The restaurant is open daily 17:30–23:30, and books through SevenRooms via inddeebkk.com or by calling +66 62 812 9696. The two-story townhouse offers both a chef's table and private rooms to book. Getting there is easier than it looks — it's about a 9-minute walk from BTS Ratchadamri, though the restaurant sits down a lane off the main Lang Suan road, so allow a little time to find the entrance, or drive and use the on-site parking

If you want to know how far Indian food can go in the hands of a 2-star chef, dinner in this old restored house is the tastiest answer you'll find

Read the full review →
blocks.signature: The 10-Destination Journey, a course that travels dish by dish across India's regions, paired with an Asia-award-winning wine pairing
mustOrder: Star Wine List award-winning wine pairing
blocks.bestFor: A special-occasion meal, and wine lovers looking to explore contemporary Indian cuisine

blocks.name: Mezzaluna
blocks.descHtml:
Mezzaluna is the crescent-moon-shaped dining room on the 65th floor of State Tower, on the Silom-riverside side of the building, where a two-story glass wall opens onto an unobstructed curve of the Chao Phraya River. In the kitchen, chef Ryuki Kawasaki cooks French food with Japanese precision, built around his signature ingredient — Murakami wagyu from Niigata, his home prefecture. The restaurant has held 2 Michelin stars continuously since the very first Thailand Michelin Guide in 2018, all the way through the 2026 edition — every single edition of the guide

The menu is entirely Chef's Tasting, choosing between 7 courses at 8,000++ THB or 9 courses at 9,600++ THB (plus 10% service and 7% VAT). Book through TableCheck with a 3,000 THB per-person deposit, deducted from your final bill — amend or cancel free up to 72 hours before your booking. The restaurant is open Monday to Saturday from 17:30, closed Sundays, with the last seating at 21:30, but regulars' trick is to book the earliest seating so you catch the sunset over the river during your meal — and allow extra time to clear the lobby security check and take the elevator up to the 65th floor. Dress is smart elegant — men need a collared shirt and long trousers, no T-shirts, sleeveless tops, shorts, or hats — and children age 7 and up are welcome. Getting there is easier than most people expect: get off at BTS Saphan Taksin and it's about a 7-minute walk to the tower

If you want a celebration meal where the food and the view are equally dramatic, book the sunset seating here and let Bangkok's lights come on course by course

Read the full review →
blocks.signature: Murakami wagyu from Niigata, within chef Ryuki Kawasaki's seasonal French-Japanese tasting menu
blocks.bestFor: A special-occasion celebration meal with a Chao Phraya River view from the 65th floor

blocks.name: Baan Tepa
blocks.descHtml:
Baan Tepa is the old family home of chef Chudaree "Tam" Debhakam on Ramkhamhaeng Road, converted into a 2-Michelin-star fine-dining restaurant that also holds a Green Star for sustainability in the 2026 Thailand guide. Chef Tam is a Top Chef Thailand champion and former sous chef at Blue Hill at Stone Barns, the famous farm restaurant in New York, and she brought that farm-to-table philosophy home for real — behind the restaurant sits Tepa Garden, where she grows the native vegetables and rare herbs used in her own kitchen. The most talked-about dish is White Lotus, a plate of assorted vegetables like jicama, lotus root, and enoki mushrooms carved and arranged into a pattern like a kaleidoscope

Before you plan a visit, know this: the restaurant is currently closed for renovation, having served its last meal on May 2, 2026, with reopening expected around August 26, 2026 — don't head out to Ramkhamhaeng right now, the house is shut. The only way to taste chef Tam's cooking this summer is the "Past • Present • Future" pop-up at F.V on Sukhumvit 39, running July 22–August 2, 2026, open Wednesday to Sunday with two seatings a day at 17:00 and 20:00, priced at 4,500++ THB (roughly 5,297 THB after charges), booked via LINE @BAANTEPA or WhatsApp +66 98 696 9074

In its normal mode, the restaurant's 7-course tasting menu runs 6,200++ THB, or roughly 7,298 THB net, serving dinner Wednesday to Sunday across three seatings — 18:00 / 19:00 / 20:00 — booked through TableCheck, which opens a 60-day window in advance. Solo diners should email reservation@baantepabkk.com instead. Worth knowing: children must be 12 or older, and there's no vegetarian or vegan version. The location sits in the Ramkhamhaeng–Bang Kapi area with no nearby train, so a taxi or Grab is the easiest way in. If you want to catch the atmosphere of the newly renovated house, follow @baantepabkk now so you don't miss the announcement when booking reopens

blocks.title: How to book a starred restaurant in time
blocks.html: Top restaurants each run their own "booking window" — Sorn opens for the following month at noon on the 25th of each month (overseas guests can email from midnight on the 15th); Sühring opens a 60-day window via SevenRooms, and weekend tables sell out within minutes. Most take a deposit or full payment and charge a no-show fee. The trick that actually works: target a weekday lunch — it's cheaper and far easier to book than dinner

blocks.title: Know before you book a starred restaurant

items.title: Book 1-3 months ahead
items.text: Three-star and two-star restaurants should be planned at least a month out, especially Friday-Saturday dinners and high season

items.title: Deposits and full prepayment are the norm
items.text: Sorn charges the full amount with no refunds under any circumstances; many restaurants deduct a no-show fee in the thousands per person. Always read the terms before confirming

items.title: Dress codes are enforced
items.text: Chef's Table turns away shorts and sandals right at the lobby; most upscale restaurants ask for smart casual or above

items.title: Check allergies/vegetarian options before you book
items.text: Some restaurants, like Sorn, can't adjust the menu at all (shellfish is central to the set). Flag any restrictions when you book

items.title: Check for temporary closures
items.text: Baan Tepa is closed for renovation until roughly late August 2026 — restaurants at this level periodically close for renovation or special closures, so check the restaurant's social pages before every trip

faq.q: How do I book a table at Sorn?
faq.a: Sorn seats about 22 and opens bookings via TableCheck at exactly noon Thailand time on the 25th of each month for the following month (moved to the 24th if the 25th falls on a Saturday). Overseas guests can email reservation@sornfinesouthern.com starting midnight on the 15th. Full payment is required at booking and cancellations aren't allowed under any circumstances. The tasting menu is 7,800++ THB per person

faq.q: How far in advance can I book Sühring?
faq.a: Book through SevenRooms up to 60 days ahead — since earning its third star, weekend tables sell out within minutes of the window opening. The shortcut is Thursday–Sunday lunch, which is far easier to book. Cancelling with less than 48 hours' notice incurs a fee of 5,800 THB per person

faq.q: What's the budget for a Michelin-starred meal in Bangkok?
faq.a: It varies widely — street-food-style one-star spots start in the hundreds to low thousands of baht, most one-star tasting menus run 2,500–5,500 THB, two-star runs roughly 6,000–9,500++ THB, and three-star runs 7,800–9,800++ THB, all before the 10% service charge, 7% tax, and wine pairing

It's temporarily closed for renovation — it served its last meal on May 2, 2026, with reopening expected around August 26, 2026. In the meantime there's a "Past • Present • Future" pop-up at F.V on Sukhumvit 39 (July 22–August 2, 2026), booked via LINE @BAANTEPA

faq.q: Which starred restaurant is easiest to book?
faq.a: At the two-star level, Chef's Table at lebua usually has availability just days to a few weeks out. Many one-star restaurants can be booked normally online or by phone, and street-food names like Jay Fai just require queuing on-site

faq.q: What should I wear to a starred restaurant?
faq.a: Most call for smart casual or above — Chef's Table is strictest: collared shirt, long trousers, no T-shirts, shorts, sandals, or hats. Sühring asks for long trousers and proper shoes. Street-food-style one-star spots let you dress casually

quickAnswerHtml: Bangkok holds 41 Michelin-starred restaurants in the 2026 guide (including Nonthaburi) — 2 three-star restaurants: Sorn (Southern Thai, booked via TableCheck opening at noon on the 25th of each month) and Sühring (German, booked via SevenRooms up to 60 days ahead); 8 two-star restaurants; and 31 one-star restaurants. Budgets range from the high hundreds of baht at Michelin street-food spots up to tens of thousands at the three-star restaurants
